# CISA Google Workspace Secure Configuration Baseline for Gmail

Gmail is the Google Workspace offering for sending and receiving email. Users can upload attachments to emails and send them to a given email address. Additional Gmail features include integrating with other Google applications, such as Meet and Chat. This Secure Configuration Baseline (SCB) provides specific policies to strengthen Gmail security.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's (CISA) Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) project provides guidance and capabilities to secure federal civilian executive branch (FCEB) agencies' cloud business application environments and protect federal information that is created, accessed, shared, and stored in those environments.

The CISA SCuBA SCBs for GWS help secure federal information assets stored within GWS cloud business application environments through consistent, effective, and manageable security configurations. CISA created baselines tailored to the federal government's threats and risk tolerance. Organizations outside of the federal government may also find these baselines to be useful references to help reduce risks even if such organizations have different risk tolerances or face different threats.

For non-federal users, the information in this document is being provided "as is" for INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service, including any subjects of analysis. Any reference to specific commercial entities or commercial products, processes, or services by service mark, trademark, manufacturer, or otherwise, does not constitute or imply endorsement, recommendation, or favoritism by CISA. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, some controls and settings are not available in all products. CISA has no control over vendor changes to products offerings or features. Accordingly, these SCuBA SCBs for GWS may not be applicable to the products available to you. This document does not address, ensure compliance with, or supersede any law, regulation, or other authority. Entities are responsible for complying with any recordkeeping, privacy, and other laws that may apply to the use of technology. This document is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit for anyone against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

This baseline is based on Google documentation available in the [Gmail Google Workspace Admin Help Center](https://support.google.com/a/topic/9202?hl=en&ref_topic=9197) and addresses the following:

- [Mail Delegation](#1-mail-delegation)

64:Mail delegation SHOULD be disabled.
65:
66:[![Automated Check](https://img.shields.io/badge/Automated_Check-5E9732)](#key-terminology)
67:
68:- _Rationale:_ Granting mail delegation can inadvertently lead to disclosure of sensitive information, impersonation of delegated accounts, or malicious alteration or deletion of emails. By controlling mail delegation, these risks can be significantly reduced, improving the security and integrity of email communications.
69:- _Last modified:_ October 2023
70:- _Note:_ Exceptions should be limited to individuals authorized by existing agency policy, such as Senior Executive Service (SES) or politically appointed staff. Other considerations include ensuring that delegated accounts require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication (MFA), limiting delegated account permissions (e.g. allowing view/reply, prohibiting delete), monitoring delegated accounts regularly, and disabling them if no longer required.

89:To configure the settings for Mail Delegation:
90:1.  Sign in to the [Google Admin Console](https://admin.google.com).
91:2.  Select **Apps -\> Google Workspace -\> Gmail**.
92:3.  Select **User Settings -\> Mail delegation**.
93:4.  Ensure that the **Let users delegate access to their mailbox to other users in the domain** checkbox is unchecked.
94:5.  Select **Save**.

97:## 2. DomainKeys Identified Mail
98:
99:This section enables DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) to help prevent spoofing of outgoing messages sent from a specific domain. DKIM allows digital signatures to be added to email messages in the message header, providing a layer of both authenticity and integrity to emails. Without DKIM, messages that are sent from a specific domain are more likely to be marked as spam by receiving mail servers. DKIM relies on Domain Name System (DNS) records and its deployment depends on how an agency manages its DNS.

<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Calls a family's InstanceSource and returns the instances to run and the rows for those that do not.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The source returns one object per instance: Id (the suffix; required, unique,
    ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$) and optional Title, Severity, Tag and Data (design section 10).
    A source that throws gives one Error row on the parent ID (InstanceSourceFailed); no instances give
    one Skipped row (NoInstances); an invalid or repeated suffix gives one Error row (InvalidInstanceId).
    Instances that an instance-level ID pattern, -ExcludeTestId or a disabled TestSettings row deselects
    get NotRun rows on their instance IDs.
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [object] $PlanRow,
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [psmoduleinfo] $Module,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [pscustomobject] $RunConfig,
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [pscustomobject] $Selection
    )

    $test = $PlanRow.Test
    $parentRow = {
        param($disposition, $code, $detail)
        $copy = [pscustomobject]@{} ; foreach ($prop in $PlanRow.PSObject.Properties) { $copy | Add-Member -NotePropertyName $prop.Name -NotePropertyValue $prop.Value }
        $copy.Disposition = $disposition; $copy.ReasonCode = $code; $copy.ReasonDetail = $detail
        ConvertTo-MtNativeRow -PlanRow $copy
    }

    $sourceItem = [Maester.Engine.MtWorkItem]::new()
    $sourceItem.Id = $test.Id
    $sourceItem.Command = $test.InstanceSource
    $sourceItem.Title = [string]$test.Title
    $sourceItem.Module = $Module
    $sourceItem.Lane = 'Main'
    if ($PlanRow.TimeoutSeconds -gt 0) { $sourceItem.TimeoutSeconds = $PlanRow.TimeoutSeconds }
    $source = @(Invoke-MtEngineRun -WorkItem $sourceItem -Module $ExecutionContext.SessionState.Module) | Select-Object -First 1
    Write-MtTestOutput -Complete
    $empty = @{ Instances = @(); PlanRows = @{} }
    switch ([string]$source.Status) {
        'Completed' { $instances = @($source.Output | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ }) }
        'Skipped' { return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Skipped' 'TestSkipped' $source.Reason) }) }
        'Timeout' {
            return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Error' 'InstanceSourceFailed' "The instance source $($test.InstanceSource) did not finish within $($PlanRow.TimeoutSeconds) seconds.") })
        }
        default {
            return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Error' 'InstanceSourceFailed' "The instance source $($test.InstanceSource) failed: $($source.Reason)") })
        }
    }
    if ($instances.Count -eq 0) {
        return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Skipped' 'NoInstances' 'There is nothing in this tenant for this test to check.') })
    }

    $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    foreach ($i in $instances) {
        $suffix = [string]$i.Id
        if ($suffix -notmatch '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}\z' -or -not $seen.Add($suffix)) {
            return [pscustomobject]($empty + @{ Rows = @(& $parentRow 'Error' 'InvalidInstanceId' "The instance source returned an invalid or repeated instance ID '$suffix'.") })
        }
    }

    $run = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $rows = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $planRows = @{}
    $copyRow = {
        $copy = [pscustomobject]@{}
        foreach ($prop in $PlanRow.PSObject.Properties) { $copy | Add-Member -NotePropertyName $prop.Name -NotePropertyValue $prop.Value }
        $copy
    }
    foreach ($i in $instances) {
        $instanceId = "$($test.Id).$($i.Id)"
        $reason = $null
        if (@($PlanRow.InstancePatterns).Count -gt 0 -and -not (Test-MtIdMatch -Id $instanceId -Pattern $PlanRow.InstancePatterns)) {
            $reason = @('NotSelected', 'Not in the list of test IDs to run.')
        } elseif ($Selection -and (Test-MtIdMatch -Id $instanceId -Pattern $Selection.ExcludeTestId)) {
            $reason = @('ExcludedById', "Excluded by ID.")
        } else {
            $setting = Get-MtTestSetting -RunConfig $RunConfig -Id $instanceId
            if ($setting -and $setting.PSObject.Properties['Enabled'] -and $setting.Enabled -eq $false) {
                $reason = @('DisabledByConfig', $(if ($setting.PSObject.Properties['Reason'] -and $setting.Reason) { [string]$setting.Reason } else { 'Disabled in the Maester config.' }))
            }
        }
        if ($reason) {
            $copy = [pscustomobject]@{}; foreach ($prop in $PlanRow.PSObject.Properties) { $copy | Add-Member -NotePropertyName $prop.Name -NotePropertyValue $prop.Value }
            $copy.Disposition = 'NotRun'; $copy.ReasonCode = $reason[0]; $copy.ReasonDetail = $reason[1]
            $rows.Add((ConvertTo-MtNativeRow -PlanRow $copy -Instance $i))
        } else {
            $own = if ($RunConfig.TestSettingsHash -and $RunConfig.TestSettingsHash.ContainsKey($instanceId)) { $RunConfig.TestSettingsHash[$instanceId] } else { $null }
            $ownParameters = if ($own -and $own.PSObject.Properties['Parameters']) { $own.Parameters } else { $null }
            $hasTimeout = $own -and $own.PSObject.Properties['TimeoutSeconds'] -and $null -ne $own.TimeoutSeconds
            if ($null -ne $ownParameters -or $hasTimeout) {
                $instanceRow = & $copyRow
                if ($null -ne $ownParameters) {
                    $configValues = @{}
                    $overrideValues = @{}
                    foreach ($e in @($PlanRow.EffectiveParameters)) {
                        if ($e.Source -eq 'Config') { $configValues[$e.Name] = $e.Value }
                        elseif ($e.Source -eq 'Parameter') { $overrideValues[$e.Name] = $e.Value }
                    }
                    if ($ownParameters -is [System.Collections.IDictionary]) { foreach ($k in $ownParameters.Keys) { $configValues[[string]$k] = $ownParameters[$k] } }
                    else { foreach ($prop in $ownParameters.PSObject.Properties) { $configValues[$prop.Name] = $prop.Value } }
                    $binding = ConvertTo-MtTestParameter -Test $test -ConfigValue $configValues -Override $overrideValues
                    $instanceRow.EffectiveParameters = $binding.Effective
                    if ($binding.Error) {
                        $instanceRow.Disposition = 'Error'; $instanceRow.ReasonCode = 'InvalidConfiguration'; $instanceRow.ReasonDetail = $binding.Error
                        $rows.Add((ConvertTo-MtNativeRow -PlanRow $instanceRow -Instance $i))
                        continue
                    }
                    $instanceRow.Parameters = $binding.Bound
                }

function Add-MtReportAttachment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Embeds an HTML report from another tool in the Maester HTML report, opened with one click.
    .DESCRIPTION
    Call this from a test, an instance source or a pack when the tool it runs writes its own single-file
    HTML report (for example the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment). The file is read at once, so the tool's
    output folder can be deleted afterwards.
    The HTML report shows a button for each attachment on the overview page, and on the result of the test
    that added it. The button shows the attached report inside the Maester report, beside its navigation, with an option to open it in a new browser tab. The report is stored compressed
    (gzip, then Base64), so a 10 MB report adds about 2 MB to the Maester report.
    Attachments are kept only in the HTML report and the results that Invoke-Maester -PassThru returns. The
    JSON results file lists each attachment's name and size without its content. The HTML report leaves
    attachments out when -RedactUserIdentity is used, because Maester cannot redact another tool's report.
    The attached page runs in a sandboxed frame, with its scripts in an origin of their own, so it cannot read or
    change the Maester report or its data. Adding a second attachment with the same name from the same test
    replaces the first.
    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path ./zt/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html
    Embeds the Zero Trust Assessment report in the Maester report of this run.
    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Tenant inventory' -Content $html
    Embeds an HTML page built in memory.
    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Add-MtReportAttachment
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'Path')]
    [OutputType([void])]
    param(
        # The label of the button that opens the attachment, for example 'Zero Trust Assessment'.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Name,
        # Path of a single-file HTML report to embed.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'Path')]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Path,
        # The HTML to embed, when it is not in a file.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ParameterSetName = 'Content')]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Content
    )
    if ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName -eq 'Path') {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Leaf)) {
            Write-Warning "Add-MtReportAttachment: $Path was not found, so '$Name' is not attached to the report."
            return
        }
        $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).ProviderPath)

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes the policy catalog of the ScubaGoggles pack from a copy of CISA's ScubaGoggles.

.DESCRIPTION
Reads the Google Workspace Secure Configuration Baselines (baselines/*.md) that ship with ScubaGoggles and writes
packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json: the ScubaGoggles version it was built from and one entry per policy, with its
requirement, criticality, indicators, rationale, NIST SP 800-53 and MITRE ATT&CK mappings and the steps to
configure it. Nothing is run.

The pack reads the catalog at run time for each result's description and remediation, which the ScubaResults
file does not hold. A policy added in a newer version of ScubaGoggles is still reported, with the text of the
results file only; rerun this script when the pack moves to a new version.

.PARAMETER SourcePath
A clone of https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles, or the installed scubagoggles package folder (the one that
holds __init__.py and baselines/). Defaults to the package of the scubagoggles command on the PATH.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Where to write the catalog. Defaults to packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json in this repository.

.EXAMPLE
./build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $SourcePath,

    [string] $OutputPath = (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..', 'packs', 'scubagoggles', 'catalog.json')
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not $SourcePath) {
    $python = Get-Command -Name python3, python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Ignore | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $python) { throw 'Python is not on the PATH. Pass -SourcePath.' }
    $SourcePath = & $python.Source -I -c 'import os, scubagoggles; print(os.path.dirname(scubagoggles.__file__))'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $SourcePath) { throw 'The scubagoggles package is not installed. Install it, or pass -SourcePath.' }
}
$packageRoot = @($SourcePath, (Join-Path $SourcePath 'scubagoggles')) |
    Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $_ '__init__.py') } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $packageRoot) { throw "No scubagoggles package (__init__.py) under $SourcePath." }
$init = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $packageRoot '__init__.py') -Raw
if ($init -notmatch "__version__\s*=\s*'([^']+)'") { throw "No __version__ in $packageRoot/__init__.py." }
$version = $Matches[1]
$baselinesPath = Join-Path $packageRoot 'baselines'

# The text of a policy's lines, without the badge lines and the blank lines around them.
function Join-MtScubaLine {
    param([string[]] $Line)
    (@($Line | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^\s*\[!\[' }) -join "`n").Trim()
}

$policies = foreach ($file in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $baselinesPath -Filter '*.md' | Where-Object Name -ne 'README.md' | Sort-Object Name) {
    $lines = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Encoding utf8)
    $product = if ($lines[0] -match 'Baseline for (.+)$') { $Matches[1].Trim() } else { $file.BaseName }
    $group = $null
    $groupNumber = $null
    $current = $null
    # The policies of the current group, and its ### Implementation section, for groups whose steps are shared.
    $groupPolicies = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $implementation = $null
    $own = @{}
    $section = $null

    $finishGroup = {
        foreach ($p in $groupPolicies) {
            $steps = if ($own.ContainsKey($p.ControlId)) { $own[$p.ControlId] } elseif ($implementation) { $implementation } else { $null }
            if ($steps) { $p.Remediation = (($steps -join "`n").Trim() -replace '\n{3,}', "`n`n") }
            $p
        }
        $groupPolicies.Clear()
    }

    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $lines.Count; $i++) {
        $line = $lines[$i]
        if ($line -match '^## (\d+)\.\s+(.+)$') {
            & $finishGroup
            $groupNumber = $Matches[1]; $group = $Matches[2].Trim()
            $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^## ') {
            & $finishGroup
            $group = $null; $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if (-not $group) { continue }
        if ($line -match '^### Implementation') { $implementation = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new(); $section = $implementation; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^### ') { $section = $null; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.[A-Z]+\.\d+\.\d+v\d+)\s+[Ii]nstructions:?\s*$') {
            $own[$Matches[1]] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $section = $own[$Matches[1]]
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.([A-Z]+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+))v(\d+)\s*$') {
            $controlId = $line.Substring(5).Trim()
            $requirement = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $j = $i + 1
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*(- _|- MITRE|####|###|\[!\[)') {
                $requirement.Add($lines[$j]); $j++
            }
            $indicators = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*- ' -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^#') {
                if ($lines[$j] -match '^\s*\[!\[([^\]]+)\]') { $indicators.Add($Matches[1]) }
                $j++
            }
            $text = Join-MtScubaLine -Line $requirement
            $criticality = if ($text -cmatch '\bSHALL\b') { 'SHALL' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bSHOULD\b') { 'SHOULD' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bMAY\b') { 'MAY' } else { $null }
            $current = [ordered]@{
                Id          = 'SCUBA.GWS.{0}.{1}.{2}' -f $Matches[2], $Matches[3], $Matches[4]
                ControlId   = $controlId
                Product     = $product
                Baseline    = $file.BaseName
                Group       = $group
                GroupNumber = $groupNumber
                Title       = ($text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
                Criticality = $criticality
                Indicators  = @($indicators | Select-Object -Unique)
                Rationale   = $null
                Note        = $null
                Nist        = @()
                Mitre       = @()
                Remediation = $null
                Url         = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/v{0}/scubagoggles/baselines/{1}#{2}' -f $version, $file.Name, ($controlId.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]', '')
            }
            $groupPolicies.Add($current)
            $section = $null
            $i = $j - 1
            continue
        }
        if ($current -and -not $section) {
            if ($line -match '^\s*- _Rationale:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Rationale = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*- _Note:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Note = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*- _NIST SP 800-53[^:]*:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Nist = @($Matches[1] -split ',\s*' | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ }) }
            elseif ($line -match 'attack\.mitre\.org/techniques/(T\d{4})(?:/(\d{3}))?') {
                $technique = if ($Matches[2]) { "$($Matches[1]).$($Matches[2])" } else { $Matches[1] }
                $current.Mitre = @($current.Mitre) + $technique | Select-Object -Unique
            }
        }
        if ($null -ne $section) { $section.Add($line) }
    }
    & $finishGroup
}

$ids = @($policies | Group-Object -Property { $_.Id } | Where-Object Count -gt 1)
if ($ids) { throw "The baselines give more than one policy the ID $($ids.Name -join ', ')." }

$catalog = [ordered]@{
    '$comment' = 'Generated by build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 from the ScubaGoggles baselines (CC0 1.0, CISA). Do not edit by hand.'
    Tool       = 'ScubaGoggles'
    Version    = $version
    Source     = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles'
    Policies   = @($policies | Sort-Object { $_.Baseline }, { [int]$_.GroupNumber }, { [int]($_.ControlId -split '\.')[3].Split('v')[0] })
}
$catalog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $OutputPath -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Information -InformationAction Continue -MessageData "Wrote $(@($policies).Count) policies from ScubaGoggles $version to $OutputPath."

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes the policy catalog of the ScubaGoggles pack from a copy of CISA's ScubaGoggles.

.DESCRIPTION
Reads the Google Workspace Secure Configuration Baselines (baselines/*.md) that ship with ScubaGoggles and writes
packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json: the ScubaGoggles version it was built from and one entry per policy, with its
requirement, criticality, indicators, rationale, NIST SP 800-53 and MITRE ATT&CK mappings and the steps to
configure it. Nothing is run.

The pack reads the catalog at run time for each result's description and remediation, which the ScubaResults
file does not hold. A policy added in a newer version of ScubaGoggles is still reported, with the text of the
results file only; rerun this script when the pack moves to a new version.

.PARAMETER SourcePath
A clone of https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles, or the installed scubagoggles package folder (the one that
holds __init__.py and baselines/). Defaults to the package of the scubagoggles command on the PATH.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Where to write the catalog. Defaults to packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json in this repository.

.EXAMPLE
./build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $SourcePath,

    [string] $OutputPath = (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..', 'packs', 'scubagoggles', 'catalog.json')
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not $SourcePath) {
    $python = Get-Command -Name python3, python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Ignore | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $python) { throw 'Python is not on the PATH. Pass -SourcePath.' }
    $SourcePath = & $python.Source -I -c 'import os, scubagoggles; print(os.path.dirname(scubagoggles.__file__))'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $SourcePath) { throw 'The scubagoggles package is not installed. Install it, or pass -SourcePath.' }
}
$packageRoot = @($SourcePath, (Join-Path $SourcePath 'scubagoggles')) |
    Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $_ '__init__.py') } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $packageRoot) { throw "No scubagoggles package (__init__.py) under $SourcePath." }
$init = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $packageRoot '__init__.py') -Raw
if ($init -notmatch "__version__\s*=\s*'([^']+)'") { throw "No __version__ in $packageRoot/__init__.py." }
$version = $Matches[1]
$baselinesPath = Join-Path $packageRoot 'baselines'

# The text of a policy's lines, without the badge lines and the blank lines around them.
function Join-MtScubaLine {
    param([string[]] $Line)
    (@($Line | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^\s*\[!\[' }) -join "`n").Trim()
}

$policies = foreach ($file in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $baselinesPath -Filter '*.md' | Where-Object Name -ne 'README.md' | Sort-Object Name) {
    $lines = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Encoding utf8)
    $product = if ($lines[0] -match 'Baseline for (.+)$') { $Matches[1].Trim() } else { $file.BaseName }
    $group = $null
    $groupNumber = $null
    $current = $null
    # The policies of the current group, and its ### Implementation section, for groups whose steps are shared.
    $groupPolicies = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $implementation = $null
    $own = @{}
    $section = $null

    $finishGroup = {
        foreach ($p in $groupPolicies) {
            $steps = if ($own.ContainsKey($p.ControlId)) { $own[$p.ControlId] } elseif ($implementation) { $implementation } else { $null }
            if ($steps) { $p.Remediation = (($steps -join "`n").Trim() -replace '\n{3,}', "`n`n") }
            $p
        }
        $groupPolicies.Clear()
    }

    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $lines.Count; $i++) {
        $line = $lines[$i]
        if ($line -match '^## (\d+)\.\s+(.+)$') {
            & $finishGroup
            $groupNumber = $Matches[1]; $group = $Matches[2].Trim()
            $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^## ') {
            & $finishGroup
            $group = $null; $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if (-not $group) { continue }
        if ($line -match '^### Implementation') { $implementation = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new(); $section = $implementation; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^### ') { $section = $null; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.[A-Z]+\.\d+\.\d+v\d+)\s+[Ii]nstructions:?\s*$') {
            $own[$Matches[1]] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $section = $own[$Matches[1]]
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.([A-Z]+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+))v(\d+)\s*$') {
            $controlId = $line.Substring(5).Trim()
            $id = 'SCUBA.GWS.{0}.{1}.{2}' -f $Matches[2], $Matches[3], $Matches[4]
            $requirement = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $j = $i + 1
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*(- _|- MITRE|####|###|\[!\[)') {
                $requirement.Add($lines[$j]); $j++
            }
            $indicators = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*- ' -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^#') {
                if ($lines[$j] -match '^\s*\[!\[([^\]]+)\]') { $indicators.Add($Matches[1]) }
                $j++
            }
            $text = Join-MtScubaLine -Line $requirement
            $criticality = if ($text -cmatch '\bSHALL\b') { 'SHALL' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bSHOULD\b') { 'SHOULD' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bMAY\b') { 'MAY' } else { $null }
            $current = [ordered]@{
                Id          = 'SCUBA.GWS.{0}.{1}.{2}' -f $Matches[2], $Matches[3], $Matches[4]
                ControlId   = $controlId
                Product     = $product
                Baseline    = $file.BaseName
                Group       = $group
                GroupNumber = $groupNumber
                Title       = ($text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
                Criticality = $criticality
                Indicators  = @($indicators | Select-Object -Unique)
                Rationale   = $null
                Note        = $null
                Nist        = @()
                Mitre       = @()
                Remediation = $null
                Url         = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/v{0}/scubagoggles/baselines/{1}#{2}' -f $version, $file.Name, ($controlId.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]', '')
            }
            $groupPolicies.Add($current)
            $section = $null
            $i = $j - 1
            continue
        }
        if ($current -and -not $section) {
            if ($line -match '^\s*- _Rationale:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Rationale = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*- _Note:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Note = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*- _NIST SP 800-53[^:]*:_\s*(.+)$') { $current.Nist = @($Matches[1] -split ',\s*' | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ }) }
            elseif ($line -match 'attack\.mitre\.org/techniques/(T\d{4})(?:/(\d{3}))?') {
                $technique = if ($Matches[2]) { "$($Matches[1]).$($Matches[2])" } else { $Matches[1] }
                $current.Mitre = @($current.Mitre) + $technique | Select-Object -Unique
            }
        }
        if ($null -ne $section) { $section.Add($line) }
    }
    & $finishGroup
}

$ids = @($policies | Group-Object -Property { $_.Id } | Where-Object Count -gt 1)
if ($ids) { throw "The baselines give more than one policy the ID $($ids.Name -join ', ')." }

$catalog = [ordered]@{
    '$comment' = 'Generated by build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 from the ScubaGoggles baselines (CC0 1.0, CISA). Do not edit by hand.'
    Tool       = 'ScubaGoggles'
    Version    = $version
    Source     = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles'
    Policies   = @($policies | Sort-Object { $_.Baseline }, { [int]$_.GroupNumber }, { [int]($_.ControlId -split '\.')[3].Split('v')[0] })
}
$catalog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $OutputPath -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Information -InformationAction Continue -MessageData "Wrote $(@($policies).Count) policies from ScubaGoggles $version to $OutputPath."

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes the policy catalog of the ScubaGoggles pack from a copy of CISA's ScubaGoggles.

.DESCRIPTION
Reads the Google Workspace Secure Configuration Baselines (baselines/*.md) that ship with ScubaGoggles and writes
packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json: the ScubaGoggles version it was built from and one entry per policy, with its
requirement, criticality, indicators, rationale, NIST SP 800-53 and MITRE ATT&CK mappings and the steps to
configure it. Nothing is run.

The pack reads the catalog at run time for each result's description and remediation, which the ScubaResults
file does not hold. A policy added in a newer version of ScubaGoggles is still reported, with the text of the
results file only; rerun this script when the pack moves to a new version.

.PARAMETER SourcePath
A clone of https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles, or the installed scubagoggles package folder (the one that
holds __init__.py and baselines/). Defaults to the package of the scubagoggles command on the PATH.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Where to write the catalog. Defaults to packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json in this repository.

.EXAMPLE
./build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $SourcePath,

    [string] $OutputPath = (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..', 'packs', 'scubagoggles', 'catalog.json')
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not $SourcePath) {
    $python = Get-Command -Name python3, python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Ignore | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $python) { throw 'Python is not on the PATH. Pass -SourcePath.' }
    $SourcePath = & $python.Source -I -c 'import os, scubagoggles; print(os.path.dirname(scubagoggles.__file__))'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $SourcePath) { throw 'The scubagoggles package is not installed. Install it, or pass -SourcePath.' }
}
$packageRoot = @($SourcePath, (Join-Path $SourcePath 'scubagoggles')) |
    Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $_ '__init__.py') } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $packageRoot) { throw "No scubagoggles package (__init__.py) under $SourcePath." }
$init = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $packageRoot '__init__.py') -Raw
if ($init -notmatch "__version__\s*=\s*'([^']+)'") { throw "No __version__ in $packageRoot/__init__.py." }
$version = $Matches[1]
$baselinesPath = Join-Path $packageRoot 'baselines'

# The text of a policy's lines, without the badge lines and the blank lines around them.
function Join-MtScubaLine {
    param([string[]] $Line)
    (@($Line | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^\s*\[!\[' }) -join "`n").Trim()
}

$policies = foreach ($file in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $baselinesPath -Filter '*.md' | Where-Object Name -ne 'README.md' | Sort-Object Name) {
    $lines = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Encoding utf8)
    $product = if ($lines[0] -match 'Baseline for (.+)$') { $Matches[1].Trim() } else { $file.BaseName }
    $group = $null
    $groupNumber = $null
    $current = $null
    # The policies of the current group, and its ### Implementation section, for groups whose steps are shared.
    $groupPolicies = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $implementation = $null
    $own = @{}
    $section = $null

    $finishGroup = {
        foreach ($p in $groupPolicies) {
            # A policy's own steps follow the steps its group shares, such as a Policy Group 1 Common Instructions section.
            $steps = @($implementation) + @(if ($own.ContainsKey($p.ControlId)) { $own[$p.ControlId] }) | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ }
            if ($steps) { $p.Remediation = (($steps -join "`n").Trim() -replace '\n{3,}', "`n`n") }
            $p
        }
        $groupPolicies.Clear()
    }

    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $lines.Count; $i++) {
        $line = $lines[$i]
        if ($line -match '^## (\d+)\.\s+(.+)$') {
            & $finishGroup
            $groupNumber = $Matches[1]; $group = $Matches[2].Trim()
            $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^## ') {
            & $finishGroup
            $group = $null; $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if (-not $group) { continue }
        if ($line -match '^### Implementation') { $implementation = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new(); $section = $implementation; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^### ') { $section = $null; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.[A-Z]+\.\d+\.\d+v\d+)\s+[Ii]nstructions:?\s*$') {
            $own[$Matches[1]] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $section = $own[$Matches[1]]
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.([A-Z]+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+))v(\d+)\s*$') {
            $controlId = $line.Substring(5).Trim()
            $id = 'SCUBA.GWS.{0}.{1}.{2}' -f $Matches[2], $Matches[3], $Matches[4]
            $requirement = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $j = $i + 1
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*(- _|- MITRE|####|###|\[!\[)') {
                $requirement.Add($lines[$j]); $j++
            }
            $indicators = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*- ' -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^#') {
                if ($lines[$j] -match '^\s*\[!\[([^\]]+)\]') { $indicators.Add($Matches[1]) }
                $j++
            }
            $text = Join-MtScubaLine -Line $requirement
            $criticality = if ($text -cmatch '\bSHALL\b') { 'SHALL' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bSHOULD\b') { 'SHOULD' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bMAY\b') { 'MAY' } else { $null }
            $current = [ordered]@{
                Id          = $id
                ControlId   = $controlId
                Product     = $product
                Baseline    = $file.BaseName
                Group       = $group
                GroupNumber = $groupNumber
                Title       = ($text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
                Criticality = $criticality
                Indicators  = @($indicators | Select-Object -Unique)
                Rationale   = $null
                Note        = $null
                Nist        = @()
                Mitre       = @()
                Remediation = $null
                Url         = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/v{0}/scubagoggles/baselines/{1}#{2}' -f $version, $file.Name, ($controlId.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]', '')
            }
            $groupPolicies.Add($current)
            $section = $null
            $i = $j - 1
            continue
        }
        if ($current -and -not $section) {
            # The baselines write both _Rationale:_ and _Rationale_:.
            if ($line -match '^\s*-\s+_Rationale(?::_|_:)\s*(.+)$') { $current.Rationale = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*-\s+_Note(?::_|_:)\s*(.+)$') { $current.Note = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*-\s+_NIST SP 800-53[^:_]*(?::_|_:)\s*(.+)$') { $current.Nist = @($Matches[1] -split ',\s*' | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ }) }
            elseif ($line -match 'attack\.mitre\.org/techniques/(T\d{4})(?:/(\d{3}))?') {
                $technique = if ($Matches[2]) { "$($Matches[1]).$($Matches[2])" } else { $Matches[1] }
                $current.Mitre = @($current.Mitre) + $technique | Select-Object -Unique
            }
        }
        if ($null -ne $section) { $section.Add($line) }
    }
    & $finishGroup
}

$ids = @($policies | Group-Object -Property { $_.Id } | Where-Object Count -gt 1)
if ($ids) { throw "The baselines give more than one policy the ID $($ids.Name -join ', ')." }

$catalog = [ordered]@{
    '$comment' = 'Generated by build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 from the ScubaGoggles baselines (CC0 1.0, CISA). Do not edit by hand.'
    Tool       = 'ScubaGoggles'
    Version    = $version
    Source     = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles'
    Policies   = @($policies | Sort-Object { $_.Baseline }, { [int]$_.GroupNumber }, { [int]($_.ControlId -split '\.')[3].Split('v')[0] })
}
$catalog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $OutputPath -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Information -InformationAction Continue -MessageData "Wrote $(@($policies).Count) policies from ScubaGoggles $version to $OutputPath."

---
title: Zero Trust Assessment pack
sidebar_position: 4
description: Run Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment from Maester and see each of its results in the Maester report.
---

# Zero Trust Assessment pack

This pack runs Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) and shows each of its
results in the Maester report, next to Maester's own checks. It ships with Maester and does not run unless you
ask for it.

Each assessment result is one row, `ZTA.<assessment test ID>` (for example `ZTA.21770`), with the
assessment's title, risk level (as the severity), description, remediation steps and findings. Results are tagged
`ZeroTrust` and `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` (`ZeroTrust.Identity`, `ZeroTrust.Devices` and so on).

The pack's ID is `maester.zero-trust-assessment`. It needs no `Install-MtPack`: it is part of the Maester module,
and `Get-MtPack` lists it.

## Run it

Install the assessment's module once, connect Maester to the tenant, then name the pack:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -SkipBuiltIn    # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA                 # Maester's tests and the assessment
```

You don't run `Connect-ZtAssessment` yourself. The assessment runs in a separate PowerShell process, which can't
use the sign-ins of your session, so Maester signs in there for you (see
[Let Maester run the assessment](#let-maester-run-the-assessment)). After an interactive `Connect-Maester` you
sign in a second time, in the browser, for the assessment. `Connect-Maester` is still needed: it tells the
assessment which tenant to sign in to, and the pack is skipped while Maester is not connected to Graph. If you
read a report you already have (below), you run `Connect-ZtAssessment` and `Invoke-ZtAssessment` yourself first.

The pack is a long-running test, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless you name it. These also run it:

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -TestId ZTA          # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Suite ZTA              # the same
Invoke-Maester -IncludeLongRunning          # everything, including the assessment
```

The pack itself stays enabled, so naming it is enough; it is the long-running flag that keeps it out of a plain
`Invoke-Maester`. To remove it entirely, set `Packs: [{ "Id": "maester.zero-trust-assessment", "Enabled": false }]`.

To run it on every run, add it to `Selection.TestId` in `maester-config.json`, or set
`Selection.IncludeLongRunning` to `true`. Give it time with `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`: the assessment
can take an hour or more on a large tenant.

The pack gets the assessment's results one of two ways.

### Read a report you already have (recommended in CI)

Run the assessment as its own step, then point Maester at the report it wrote:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-ZtAssessment
Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path ./zt -NoBrowser
```

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath": "./zt" } }
```

Then, in a new PowerShell session (the assessment's modules can't share one with Maester's), connect Maester to
the same tenant and run the pack:

```powershell
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA
```

`ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` takes the report file (`ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json`), the folder given to
`Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path`, or its `zt-export` folder. Maester refuses a report written for another tenant than the
one it is connected to, and one older than `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` (7 by default; 0 turns the check
off).

### Let Maester run the assessment

Without `ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath`, Maester runs the assessment itself. Install the module first:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
```

The assessment loads its own versions of the Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online and Az modules, which cannot share
a PowerShell session with the ones Maester has loaded. So Maester starts it in a separate `pwsh` process, which
signs in with `Connect-ZtAssessment`:

- It signs in to the tenant Maester is connected to.
- When Maester is connected to Graph app-only with a certificate, it uses the same app and certificate. The app
  needs the Graph application permissions that `Get-ZtGraphScope` lists.
- When Maester is connected app-only another way (a client secret, a managed identity or workload identity
  federation), the pack is skipped with the reason: the assessment signs in app-only only with a certificate. See
  [Run it in a pipeline](#run-it-in-a-pipeline).
- Otherwise it signs in interactively, so you sign in a second time. Without a browser, for example over SSH, set
  `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "UseDeviceCode": true }`.

While it runs, what the assessment writes is shown live: in the full-screen dashboard of an interactive run it
scrolls in a box in the middle of the screen, under the phases of the run, and in other modes (CI, redirected
output, `-Verbosity Normal`) it is written to the console, indented. The assessment runs with `-ShowLog`, so it lists
the tests it runs, and its progress bars become one line at the bottom of the box that updates in place. Set
`ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog` to `false` for its shorter output.

The top of the box shows where the assessment is, read once a second from the progress the assessment keeps for
its own progress page and from the progress logs it writes in its output folder:

- the six stages of the assessment as a track (Export, Tests, Tenant info, Results, Report data, HTML report),
  with the step of the stage it is on, such as "Importing Data into Database";
- a bar of the exports or tests done of how many, the percentage, how many failed and are running, and the time
  left;
- each export or test that is running, with what it is doing and how long it has run, and the ones that finished,
  with their result and how long they took, listed the way the dashboard lists Maester's own tests (tests by
  their `ZTA.` ID and title);
- each export, database import or test that fails or times out, with its error. The box counts them.

The rest of the dashboard follows the assessment while it runs:

- the Results panel and the result blocks over the box count the assessment's results (passed, failed,
  investigate, skipped) as its tests finish;
- the assessment's pillars are listed where Maester's products usually are, each with a bar and its counts;
- the Pace graph next to the logo draws how long each export and test took, and the Slowest panel lists the
  slowest of them.

Outside the dashboard the stage is written when it changes, each export and test as it finishes with its result
and time, the counts at most every ten seconds, and each failure as it happens. This needs version 3.1 or later of the ZeroTrustAssessment module; with an earlier version the
box shows the log only.

The assessment's own report and raw export go to a temporary folder that Maester deletes after reading it, because
the export holds tenant data. Set `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` to keep them.

## Run it in a pipeline

In GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps or any other pipeline, nobody is there to sign in, so the assessment signs in
as a service principal. `Connect-ZtAssessment` signs in app-only only with a certificate, found by thumbprint in
the certificate store of the computer it runs on. A client secret, a managed identity or workload identity
federation (the OIDC sign-in in [Maester's GitHub guide](../monitoring/github.md)) is enough for Maester's own
tests but not for the assessment.

So the pipeline needs:

1. An app registration with a certificate. Give the app the Graph application permissions that
   `Get-ZtGraphScope` lists (run it after `Import-Module ZeroTrustAssessment`), plus Maester's own permissions if
   the same run includes Maester's tests. The assessment's Azure, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and
   SharePoint tests need the app to have the roles the
   [Zero Trust Assessment documentation](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) lists for app-only sign-in; to
   leave those services out, set `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "Service": ["Graph"] }`.
2. The certificate as a PFX file, saved base64-encoded in a pipeline secret with its password.
3. A step that adds the certificate to the current user's certificate store, connects Maester to Graph with it
   by thumbprint, and runs the pack. The child process finds the same certificate by its thumbprint.

A GitHub Actions workflow that does this on a schedule, with the secrets `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`,
`ZTA_CERTIFICATE` (the base64 PFX) and `ZTA_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`:

```yaml
name: Zero Trust Assessment
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  zero-trust:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 360
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run the Zero Trust Assessment with Maester
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.ZTA_CERTIFICATE }}
          CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ZTA_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          Install-Module Maester, ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser -Force

          # Add the certificate to the current user's store, where the assessment looks for it.
          $flags = 'PersistKeySet, Exportable'
          $cert = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2]::new(
              [Convert]::FromBase64String($env:CERTIFICATE), $env:CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD, $flags)
          $store = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Store]::new('My', 'CurrentUser')
          $store.Open('ReadWrite'); $store.Add($cert); $store.Close()

          Connect-MgGraph -ClientId $env:CLIENT_ID -TenantId $env:TENANT_ID -CertificateThumbprint $cert.Thumbprint -NoWelcome
          Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -NonInteractive -OutputFolder ./test-results

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: maester-zero-trust
          path: test-results

---
title: Zero Trust Assessment pack
sidebar_position: 4
description: Run Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment from Maester and see each of its results in the Maester report.
---

# Zero Trust Assessment pack

This pack runs Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) and shows each of its
results in the Maester report, next to Maester's own checks. It ships with Maester and does not run unless you
ask for it.

Each assessment result is one row, `ZTA.<assessment test ID>` (for example `ZTA.21770`), with the
assessment's title, risk level (as the severity), description, remediation steps and findings. Results are tagged
`ZeroTrust` and `ZeroTrust.<pillar>` (`ZeroTrust.Identity`, `ZeroTrust.Devices` and so on).

The pack's ID is `maester.zero-trust-assessment`. It needs no `Install-MtPack`: it is part of the Maester module,
and `Get-MtPack` lists it.

## Run it

Install the assessment's module once, connect Maester to the tenant, then name the pack:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -SkipBuiltIn    # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA                 # Maester's tests and the assessment
```

You don't run `Connect-ZtAssessment` yourself. The assessment runs in a separate PowerShell process, which can't
use the sign-ins of your session, so Maester signs in there for you (see
[Let Maester run the assessment](#let-maester-run-the-assessment)). After an interactive `Connect-Maester` you
sign in a second time, in the browser, for the assessment. `Connect-Maester` is still needed: it tells the
assessment which tenant to sign in to, and the pack is skipped while Maester is not connected to Graph. If you
read a report you already have (below), you run `Connect-ZtAssessment` and `Invoke-ZtAssessment` yourself first.

The pack is a long-running test, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless you name it. These also run it:

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -TestId ZTA          # only the Zero Trust Assessment
Invoke-Maester -Suite ZTA              # the same
Invoke-Maester -IncludeLongRunning          # everything, including the assessment
```

The pack itself stays enabled, so naming it is enough; it is the long-running flag that keeps it out of a plain
`Invoke-Maester`. To remove it entirely, set `Packs: [{ "Id": "maester.zero-trust-assessment", "Enabled": false }]`.

To run it on every run, add it to `Selection.TestId` in `maester-config.json`, or set
`Selection.IncludeLongRunning` to `true`. Give it time with `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`: the assessment
can take an hour or more on a large tenant.

The pack gets the assessment's results one of two ways.

### Read a report you already have (recommended in CI)

Run the assessment as its own step, then point Maester at the report it wrote:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-ZtAssessment
Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path ./zt -NoBrowser
```

```json
{ "GlobalSettings": { "ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath": "./zt" } }
```

Then, in a new PowerShell session (the assessment's modules can't share one with Maester's), connect Maester to
the same tenant and run the pack:

```powershell
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA
```

`ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath` takes the report file (`ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json`), the folder given to
`Invoke-ZtAssessment -Path`, or its `zt-export` folder. Maester refuses a report written for another tenant than the
one it is connected to, and one older than `ZeroTrustAssessment.MaxReportAgeDays` (7 by default; 0 turns the check
off).

### Let Maester run the assessment

Without `ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath`, Maester runs the assessment itself. Install the module first:

```powershell
Install-Module ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser
```

The assessment loads its own versions of the Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online and Az modules, which cannot share
a PowerShell session with the ones Maester has loaded. So Maester starts it in a separate `pwsh` process, which
signs in with `Connect-ZtAssessment`:

- It signs in to the tenant Maester is connected to.
- When Maester is connected to Graph app-only with a certificate, it uses the same app and certificate. The app
  needs the Graph application permissions that `Get-ZtGraphScope` lists.
- When Maester is connected app-only another way (a client secret, a managed identity or workload identity
  federation), the pack is skipped with the reason: the assessment signs in app-only only with a certificate. See
  [Run it in a pipeline](#run-it-in-a-pipeline).
- Otherwise it signs in interactively, so you sign in a second time. Without a browser, for example over SSH, set
  `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "UseDeviceCode": true }`.

While it runs, what the assessment writes is shown live: in the full-screen dashboard of an interactive run it
scrolls in a box in the middle of the screen, under the phases of the run, and in other modes (CI, redirected
output, `-Verbosity Normal`) it is written to the console, indented. The assessment runs with `-ShowLog`, so it lists
the tests it runs, and its progress bars become one line at the bottom of the box that updates in place. Set
`ZeroTrustAssessment.ShowLog` to `false` for its shorter output.

The top of the box shows where the assessment is, read once a second from the progress the assessment keeps for
its own progress page and from the progress logs it writes in its output folder:

- the six stages of the assessment as a track (Export, Tests, Tenant info, Results, Report data, HTML report),
  with the step of the stage it is on, such as "Importing Data into Database";
- a bar of the exports or tests done of how many, the percentage, how many failed and are running, and the time
  left;
- each export or test that is running, with what it is doing and how long it has run, and the ones that finished,
  with their result and how long they took, listed the way the dashboard lists Maester's own tests (tests by
  their `ZTA.` ID and title);
- each export, database import or test that fails or times out, with its error. The box counts them.

The rest of the dashboard follows the assessment while it runs:

- the Results panel and the result blocks over the box count the assessment's results (passed, failed,
  investigate, skipped) as its tests finish;
- the assessment's pillars are listed where Maester's products usually are, each with a bar and its counts;
- the Pace graph next to the logo draws how long each export and test took, and the Slowest panel lists the
  slowest of them.

Outside the dashboard the stage is written when it changes, each export and test as it finishes with its result
and time, the counts at most every ten seconds, and each failure as it happens. This needs version 3.1 or later of the ZeroTrustAssessment module; with an earlier version the
box shows the log only.

The assessment's own report and raw export go to a temporary folder that Maester deletes after reading it, because
the export holds tenant data. Set `ZeroTrustAssessment.OutputPath` to keep them.

## Run it in a pipeline

In GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps or any other pipeline, nobody is there to sign in, so the assessment signs in
as a service principal. `Connect-ZtAssessment` signs in app-only only with a certificate, found by thumbprint in
the certificate store of the computer it runs on. A client secret, a managed identity or workload identity
federation (the OIDC sign-in in [Maester's GitHub guide](../monitoring/github.md)) is enough for Maester's own
tests but not for the assessment.

So the pipeline needs:

1. An app registration with a certificate. Give the app the Graph application permissions that
   `Get-ZtGraphScope` lists (run it after `Import-Module ZeroTrustAssessment`), plus Maester's own permissions if
   the same run includes Maester's tests. The assessment's Azure, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance and
   SharePoint tests need the app to have the roles the
   [Zero Trust Assessment documentation](https://aka.ms/zerotrust/assessment) lists for app-only sign-in; to
   leave those services out, set `ZeroTrustAssessment.Connect` to `{ "Service": ["Graph"] }`.
2. The certificate as a PFX file, saved base64-encoded in a pipeline secret with its password.
3. A step that adds the certificate to the current user's certificate store, connects Maester to Graph with it
   by thumbprint, and runs the pack. The child process finds the same certificate by its thumbprint.

A GitHub Actions workflow that does this on a schedule, with the secrets `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`,
`ZTA_CERTIFICATE` (the base64 PFX) and `ZTA_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`:

```yaml
name: Zero Trust Assessment
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  zero-trust:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 360
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run the Zero Trust Assessment with Maester
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.ZTA_CERTIFICATE }}
          CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ZTA_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          Install-Module Maester, ZeroTrustAssessment -Scope CurrentUser -Force

          # Add the certificate to the current user's store, where the assessment looks for it.
          $flags = 'PersistKeySet, Exportable'
          $cert = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2]::new(
              [Convert]::FromBase64String($env:CERTIFICATE), $env:CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD, $flags)
          $store = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Store]::new('My', 'CurrentUser')
          $store.Open('ReadWrite'); $store.Add($cert); $store.Close()

          Connect-MgGraph -ClientId $env:CLIENT_ID -TenantId $env:TENANT_ID -CertificateThumbprint $cert.Thumbprint -NoWelcome
          Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA -NonInteractive -OutputFolder ./test-results

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: maester-zero-trust
          path: test-results
```

Maester's step can then connect any way it likes, including OIDC, as long as it is the same tenant.

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes the policy catalog of the ScubaGoggles pack from a copy of CISA's ScubaGoggles.

.DESCRIPTION
Reads the Google Workspace Secure Configuration Baselines (baselines/*.md) that ship with ScubaGoggles and writes
packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json: the ScubaGoggles version it was built from and one entry per policy (Tests, the
shape the pack index reads), with its requirement, criticality and the severity the pack gives it, indicators, rationale, NIST SP 800-53 and MITRE ATT&CK mappings and the steps to
configure it. Nothing is run.

The pack reads the catalog at run time for each result's description and remediation, which the ScubaResults
file does not hold. A policy added in a newer version of ScubaGoggles is still reported, with the text of the
results file only; rerun this script when the pack moves to a new version.

.PARAMETER SourcePath
A clone of https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles, or the installed scubagoggles package folder (the one that
holds __init__.py and baselines/). Defaults to the package of the scubagoggles command on the PATH.

.PARAMETER OutputPath
Where to write the catalog. Defaults to packs/scubagoggles/catalog.json in this repository.

.EXAMPLE
./build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $SourcePath,

    [string] $OutputPath = (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..', 'packs', 'scubagoggles', 'catalog.json')
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

if (-not $SourcePath) {
    $python = Get-Command -Name python3, python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Ignore | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $python) { throw 'Python is not on the PATH. Pass -SourcePath.' }
    $SourcePath = & $python.Source -I -c 'import os, scubagoggles; print(os.path.dirname(scubagoggles.__file__))'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not $SourcePath) { throw 'The scubagoggles package is not installed. Install it, or pass -SourcePath.' }
}
$packageRoot = @($SourcePath, (Join-Path $SourcePath 'scubagoggles')) |
    Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $_ '__init__.py') } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $packageRoot) { throw "No scubagoggles package (__init__.py) under $SourcePath." }
$init = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $packageRoot '__init__.py') -Raw
if ($init -notmatch "__version__\s*=\s*'([^']+)'") { throw "No __version__ in $packageRoot/__init__.py." }
$version = $Matches[1]
$baselinesPath = Join-Path $packageRoot 'baselines'

# The text of a policy's lines, without the badge lines and the blank lines around them.
function Join-MtScubaLine {
    param([string[]] $Line)
    (@($Line | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^\s*\[!\[' }) -join "`n").Trim()
}

$policies = foreach ($file in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $baselinesPath -Filter '*.md' | Where-Object Name -ne 'README.md' | Sort-Object Name) {
    $lines = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Encoding utf8)
    $product = if ($lines[0] -match 'Baseline for (.+)$') { $Matches[1].Trim() } else { $file.BaseName }
    $group = $null
    $groupNumber = $null
    $current = $null
    # The policies of the current group, and its ### Implementation section, for groups whose steps are shared.
    $groupPolicies = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $implementation = $null
    $own = @{}
    $section = $null

    $finishGroup = {
        foreach ($p in $groupPolicies) {
            # A policy's own steps follow the steps its group shares, such as a Policy Group 1 Common Instructions section.
            # Their headings become bold lines, so they don't outrank the headings of the Maester report.
            $steps = @($implementation) + @(if ($own.ContainsKey($p.ControlId)) { $own[$p.ControlId] }) | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ } |
                ForEach-Object { $_ -replace '^#{3,}\s+(.+?):?\s*$', '**$1**' }
            if ($steps) { $p.Remediation = (($steps -join "`n").Trim() -replace '\n{3,}', "`n`n") }
            $p
        }
        $groupPolicies.Clear()
    }

    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $lines.Count; $i++) {
        $line = $lines[$i]
        if ($line -match '^## (\d+)\.\s+(.+)$') {
            & $finishGroup
            $groupNumber = $Matches[1]; $group = $Matches[2].Trim()
            $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^## ') {
            & $finishGroup
            $group = $null; $implementation = $null; $own = @{}; $section = $null; $current = $null
            continue
        }
        if (-not $group) { continue }
        if ($line -match '^### Implementation') { $implementation = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new(); $section = $implementation; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^### ') { $section = $null; $current = $null; continue }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.[A-Z]+\.\d+\.\d+v\d+)\s+[Ii]nstructions:?\s*$') {
            $own[$Matches[1]] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $section = $own[$Matches[1]]
            continue
        }
        if ($line -match '^#### (GWS\.([A-Z]+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+))v(\d+)\s*$') {
            $controlId = $line.Substring(5).Trim()
            $id = 'SCUBA.GWS.{0}.{1}.{2}' -f $Matches[2], $Matches[3], $Matches[4]
            $requirement = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            $j = $i + 1
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*(- _|- MITRE|####|###|\[!\[)') {
                $requirement.Add($lines[$j]); $j++
            }
            $indicators = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
            while ($j -lt $lines.Count -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^\s*- ' -and $lines[$j] -notmatch '^#') {
                if ($lines[$j] -match '^\s*\[!\[([^\]]+)\]') { $indicators.Add($Matches[1]) }
                $j++
            }
            $text = Join-MtScubaLine -Line $requirement
            $criticality = if ($text -cmatch '\bSHALL\b') { 'SHALL' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bSHOULD\b') { 'SHOULD' } elseif ($text -cmatch '\bMAY\b') { 'MAY' } else { $null }
            $current = [ordered]@{
                Id          = $id
                ControlId   = $controlId
                Product     = $product
                Baseline    = $file.BaseName
                Group       = $group
                GroupNumber = $groupNumber
                Title       = ($text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
                Criticality = $criticality
                Severity    = switch ($criticality) { 'SHALL' { 'High' } 'SHOULD' { 'Medium' } 'MAY' { 'Low' } default { $null } }
                Category    = $product
                Indicators  = @($indicators | Select-Object -Unique)
                Rationale   = $null
                Note        = $null
                Nist        = @()
                Mitre       = @()
                Remediation = $null
                Url         = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/v{0}/scubagoggles/baselines/{1}#{2}' -f $version, $file.Name, ($controlId.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]', '')
            }
            $groupPolicies.Add($current)
            $section = $null
            $i = $j - 1
            continue
        }
        if ($current -and -not $section) {
            # The baselines write both _Rationale:_ and _Rationale_:.
            if ($line -match '^\s*-\s+_Rationale(?::_|_:)\s*(.+)$') { $current.Rationale = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*-\s+_Note(?::_|_:)\s*(.+)$') { $current.Note = $Matches[1].Trim() }
            elseif ($line -match '^\s*-\s+_NIST SP 800-53[^:_]*(?::_|_:)\s*(.+)$') { $current.Nist = @($Matches[1] -split ',\s*' | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ }) }
            elseif ($line -match 'attack\.mitre\.org/techniques/(T\d{4})(?:/(\d{3}))?') {
                $technique = if ($Matches[2]) { "$($Matches[1]).$($Matches[2])" } else { $Matches[1] }
                $current.Mitre = @($current.Mitre) + $technique | Select-Object -Unique
            }
        }
        if ($null -ne $section) { $section.Add($line) }
    }
    & $finishGroup
}

$ids = @($policies | Group-Object -Property { $_.Id } | Where-Object Count -gt 1)
if ($ids) { throw "The baselines give more than one policy the ID $($ids.Name -join ', ')." }

$catalog = [ordered]@{
    '$comment' = 'Generated by build/scubagoggles/Update-MtScubaGogglesCatalog.ps1 from the ScubaGoggles baselines (CC0 1.0, CISA). Do not edit by hand.'
    Tool       = 'ScubaGoggles'
    Version    = $version
    Source     = 'https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles'
    Tests      = @($policies | Sort-Object { $_.Baseline }, { [int]$_.GroupNumber }, { [int]($_.ControlId -split '\.')[3].Split('v')[0] })
}
$catalog | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $OutputPath -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Information -InformationAction Continue -MessageData "Wrote $(@($policies).Count) policies from ScubaGoggles $version to $OutputPath."

  "NoResultReason": "ScubaGoggles did not report a result for this policy."

Reports each result of [CISA ScubaGoggles](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles), which checks a Google
Workspace tenant against CISA's Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) baselines for Google Workspace.

Each policy is its own row, `SCUBA.GWS.<product>.<group>.<policy>` (for example `SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.1.1` for
`GWS.GMAIL.1.1v1`), with the baseline's rationale, the steps to configure it and what ScubaGoggles found.

#### Running it

The pack does not run by default. Run `scubagoggles gws`, set the `ScubaGoggles.ReportPath` setting to the
results it wrote, then run `Invoke-Maester -Pack SCUBA.GWS`.

{

  "TestDescription": "**GWS.GMAIL.1.1v1** (SHOULD) · Gmail › Mail Delegation

Granting mail delegation can inadvertently lead to disclosure of sensitive information, impersonation of delegated accounts, or malicious alteration or deletion of emails. By controlling mail delegation, these risks can be significantly reduced, improving the security and integrity of email communications.

_Note:_ Exceptions should be limited to individuals authorized by existing agency policy, such as Senior Executive Service (SES) or politically appointed staff. Other considerations include ensuring that delegated accounts require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication (MFA), limiting delegated account permissions (e.g. allowing view/reply, prohibiting delete), monitoring delegated accounts regularly, and disabling them if no longer required.

#### Remediation

To configure the settings for Mail Delegation:
1.  Sign in to the [Google Admin Console](https://admin.google.com).
2.  Select **Apps -\> Google Workspace -\> Gmail**.
3.  Select **User Settings -\> Mail delegation**.
4.  Ensure that the **Let users delegate access to their mailbox to other users in the domain** checkbox is unchecked.
5.  Select **Save**.

===== SCUBA.GWS.GMAIL.3.1 Failed 
ScubaGoggles,GWS.GMAIL,BOD-25-01
{
  "Severity": "",
  "TestDescription": "**GWS.GMAIL.3.1v1** (SHALL) · Gmail › Sender Policy Framework

Threat actors could potentially manipulate an email "from" field to appear as a legitimate sender, increasing the risk of phishing attacks. By publishing an SPF policy that fails all non-approved senders for each domain, this risk can be reduced as it helps to detect and block deceptive emails. Additionally, an SPF policy is required for FCEB agencies by BOD 18-01.

#### Remediation

First, identify any approved senders specific to your agency (see [Identify all email senders for your organization](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10686639#senders) for tips). SPF allows you to indicate approved senders by IP address or CIDR range. However, note that SPF allows you to [include](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208#section-5.2) the IP addresses indicated by a separate SPF policy, refered to by domain name. See [Define your SPF record—Basic setup](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10685031) for inclusions required for Google to send email on behalf of your domain.

SPF is not configured through the Google Workspace admin center, but rather via DNS records hosted by the agency's domain. Thus, the exact steps needed to set up SPF varies from agency to agency. See [Add your SPF record at your domain provider](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10684623) for more details.

To test your SPF configuration, consider using a web-based tool, such as the [Google Admin Toolbox](https://toolbox.googleapps.com/apps/checkmx/).  Additionally, SPF records can be requested using the command line tool `dig`. For example:
```
dig example.com txt
```
If SPF is configured, a response resembling `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com -all` will be returned; though by necessity, the contents of the SPF policy may vary by agency. In this example, the SPF policy indicates the IP addresses listed by the policy for "_spf.google.com" are the only approved senders for "example.com." These IPs can be determined via additional SPF lookups, starting with "_spf.google.com."

Ensure the IP addresses listed as approved senders for your domains are correct. Additionally, ensure that each policy either ends in `-all` or [redirects](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208#section-6.1) to one that does; this directive indicates that all IPs that don't match the policy should fail. See [Define your SPF record—Advanced setup](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10683907) for a more in-depth discussion of SPF record syntax.

[CISA baseline](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles/blob/v1.1.0/scubagoggles/baselines/gmail.md#gwsgmail31v1) · NIST SP 800-53: AC-2d · MITRE ATT&CK: T1078, T1078.004, T1566, T1566.001, T1566.002, T1566.003, T1672, T1598, T1598.003",

{

  "TestDescription": "**GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.2.1v1** (SHOULD) · Common Controls › Context-aware Access

Granular device access control afforded by context-aware access aligns with federal zero trust strategy and principles. Context-aware access can help to increase the security of GWS data by allowing organizations to restrict access to certain applications or services based on user/device attributes.

_Note:_ Agencies may use controls with greater granularity if needed.

#### Remediation

{

  "TestDescription": "**GWS.GMAIL.3.1v1** (SHALL) · Gmail › Sender Policy Framework

Threat actors could potentially manipulate an email "from" field to appear as a legitimate sender, increasing the risk of phishing attacks. By publishing an SPF policy that fails all non-approved senders for each domain, this risk can be reduced as it helps to detect and block deceptive emails. Additionally, an SPF policy is required for FCEB agencies by BOD 18-01.

#### Remediation

First, identify any approved senders specific to your agency (see [Identify all email senders for your organization](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10686639#senders) for tips). SPF allows you to indicate approved senders by IP address or CIDR range. However, note that SPF allows you to [include](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208#section-5.2) the IP addresses indicated by a separate SPF policy, refered to by domain name. See [Define your SPF record—Basic setup](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10685031) for inclusions required for Google to send email on behalf of your domain.

SPF is not configured through the Google Workspace admin center, but rather via DNS records hosted by the agency's domain. Thus, the exact steps needed to set up SPF varies from agency to agency. See [Add your SPF record at your domain provider](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10684623) for more details.

To test your SPF configuration, consider using a web-based tool, such as the [Google Admin Toolbox](https://toolbox.googleapps.com/apps/checkmx/).  Additionally, SPF records can be requested using the command line tool `dig`. For example:
```
dig example.com txt
```
If SPF is configured, a response resembling `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com -all` will be returned; though by necessity, the contents of the SPF policy may vary by agency. In this example, the SPF policy indicates the IP addresses listed by the policy for "_spf.google.com" are the only approved senders for "example.com." These IPs can be determined via additional SPF lookups, starting with "_spf.google.com."

Ensure the IP addresses listed as approved senders for your domains are correct. Additionally, ensure that each policy either ends in `-all` or [redirects](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7208#section-6.1) to one that does; this directive indicates that all IPs that don't match the policy should fail. See [Define your SPF record—Advanced setup](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10683907) for a more in-depth discussion of SPF record syntax.

A setting whose name looks like a secret (`Secret`, `Password`, `Token`, `Key`, `Credential`, `Certificate`) is
never read from the config: pass it with `-ServiceSetting` or an environment variable. Pack services are never
part of `-Service All`. `Disconnect-Maester` disconnects them too.

## Packs that ship with Maester

Packs that ship with Maester are part of the module, in its `packs` folder. They are trusted as the module is:
they need no lock entry and no approval. Each one says whether it is on by default; turn one on or off with its
`Packs` entry in the config. If a pack that ships with Maester uses PowerShell Gallery modules, run
`Install-MtPack <id>` once to save them and pin their digests. Their test IDs have no `MP.` prefix: the Zero
Trust Assessment pack's tests are `ZTA.<n>`.

## Writing a pack

See [Writing a pack](./writing-a-pack.md). To learn what Maester checks and why, see
[Pack security](./security.md).
